name: QCTrojan-Bench
description: QCTrojan-Bench is a reproducible benchmark dataset and evaluation pipeline for software-level, pre-execution detection of malicious quantum circuits. It accompanies the manuscript "Software-Level Detection of Malicious Quantum Circuits: An Empirical Study" (Ajmal, Halunen, Khan; submitted to Empirical Software Engineering). Contents: 9,000 quantum circuits across five algorithm families (Deutsch–Jozsa, Grover, QAOA, VQC, QFT), each with a benign implementation and two tampered variants (static and triggered Trojans), plus a 39-dimensional normalized structural feature set, source-stratified CV split index, and full evaluation pipeline (Random Forest, Linear/RBF SVM, QSVM proof-of-concept). Licensing: dataset and results (CC BY 4.0, this deposit's license) cover circuit files, features, and results. Code and notebooks included in the archive are separately licensed under MIT — see LICENSE within the archive. This release (v1.0) corresponds to the manuscript version submitted for review. See the accompanying GitHub repository for the latest code: https://github.com/xeeshanajmal/quantum-circuit-trojan-detection
